parsed.attack: Amazon Glow [49] was built for this precise bond - grandparents and grandchildren separated by distance - and was discontinued within about a year on poor sales, and its cause was not only the $300 box: it was "changing customer behaviour", the middle generation's supply of attention that the pandemic inflated and normal life deflated. Sunday Post sits entirely downstream of that same supply, since it writes up "three photographs the parents already shared this week", and the idea's own second kill criterion concedes the failure mode outright - parents supplying fewer than five photos a week in more than half of households by week six. Long context assembles material cheaply; it produces none, and the gift structure means the person who must keep feeding it is neither the payer nor the reader, which is the weakest possible position for the one indispensable actor.
parsed.strongest_defence: Removing the hardware removes Glow's actual cost of failure and its returns risk, and unlike Glow the supply step already happens in the family WhatsApp group - the product reads a stream that exists rather than asking anyone to adopt a new ritual on a schedule.
parsed.verdict_reason: Glow's hardware and pandemic-timing causes are genuinely dissolved, but its supply-side cause - the busy middle generation not feeding the thing - is untouched and is restated as the idea's own kill condition.
